sections.html:
Murray County is in the mountains and valleys of northwest Georgia and is part of the Dalton metro area. Chatsworth is the county seat and the only city, and Eton is a town. Spring Place, Carters, Tennga, Cisco and Crandall are unincorporated communities. An address inside Chatsworth or Eton may carry city tax on top of the county bill, so ask which taxing districts cover your parcel.

About 73.8% of Murray County homes are owner-occupied, so most sales involve a seller who has been paying the county bill directly or through an escrow account. Knowing which of those applies to you is the first step before listing.

An estimated 41,607 people lived here in July 2025, and owners valued their homes at a median of $180,700 across 2020 to 2024.

sections.h2: Who to call about Murray County property tax
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner is at 101 S 3rd Ave in Chatsworth. The mailing address is P.O. Box 336, Chatsworth, GA 30705. Card and e-check payments run through a third-party company's site, and you can also pay by phone at 470-289-4681. That site offers digital statements and automated reminders.

The main county number is (706) 517-1400. Press extension 1 for the Tax Commissioner and extension 2 for the assessors. The two offices do separate jobs: the assessors set values and never collect the tax.

Deeds and recorded liens live with a different office. The Clerk of Superior Court is in the courthouse at 114 N. Third Ave, across the street from the commissioner. The clerk holds warranty deeds, which you may need for a sale.

Real estate and business personal property tax are normally due December 1, earlier than the statewide default. Manufactured homes come due May 1, and vehicle renewals follow the owner's birthday.

  • Interest runs at 1% a month once December 1 passes.
  • Balances still open 90 days later add a 10% penalty.
  • A homesteaded parcel owing under $500 is spared that 90 day penalty.
  • Past 90 days, the clerk's office can record a FiFa that credit bureaus may pick up.
  • The commissioner may levy on the property, which the office treats as a last resort.

Your printed bill controls the exact amount. If a former owner still gets a bill or notice, they may forward it to the new owner.

Homestead exemptions are filed with the assessors, not the commissioner, at (706) 517-1400, extension 2. Bring documentation of ownership. Elderly exemptions also require income verification.

  • Regular homestead: you must own and live in the home on January 1. No income test applies, and you can file online.
  • Elderly exemptions: several versions with different ages, filed in the office or by mail because of income checks.
  • Homestead freeze: available after one year of homestead, applied for in the office.
  • Disabled veteran: the taxpayer must be 100% disabled during war, with VA documentation.
  • Low income: household income below $15,000 a year, with documents.
  • Special assessments: Conservation Use, Preferential Assessment and Forest Land Protection, applied for January 1 through April 1.

Manufactured home owners who also own the land can claim homestead, pick up a free decal between January 1 and May 1, and pay the home's tax with the land tax. Other manufactured homes, such as rentals, buy a decal.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Murray County value?
sections.html:
Send a letter to the assessors within 45 days of the Notice of Property Value Change. Certified mail or hand delivery is the safest route. Explain as fully as you can why the value looks wrong, and attach any appraisal or comparable sales you have.

The Board of Assessors reviews the letter and replies in writing. From there the challenge can go to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, again within 45 days of the notice, and superior court is open afterward by written notice to the assessors.

A state-certified five-member board updates county values every year at 40% of market value. Notices and bills go to the owner of record on January 1.

Ownership on January 1 sets liability, so a seller who closes later in the year still answers for the full bill. The state gives no refund for part of a year, which means the sales contract decides how the bill is split.

Before closing, call extension 1 and ask the Tax Commissioner for the balance on your parcel and any FiFa. If your lender pays from an escrow account, ask whether it has paid, because collection questions go to the commissioner and not the assessors. If you need a copy of a warranty deed, walk across to the Clerk of Superior Court.

A rough order of work for a seller: confirm the balance, confirm which exemptions are on the account, order the deed copy if needed, then give the figures to the closing attorney. A cash sale skips the lender's review and any appraisal delay, though whatever is owed still comes out of the proceeds at closing.

Pick the payment route that fits: the third-party online site for card or e-check, the phone line at 470-289-4681, mail to the P.O. box, or a visit to the office on South 3rd Avenue. Keep a record of the payment date, especially close to December 1, since interest starts the day after.

For an exemption or appeal, bring proof of ownership, a photo ID, and for elderly or low income exemptions the income documents the assessors ask for. Calling ahead on extension 2 saves a second trip. If you plan to sell soon, file anything you are entitled to before the January 1 to April 1 window closes, since a lower bill makes the house easier to price.

If a bill goes unpaid past the dates above, the next step is the 10% penalty, then the FiFa, then possible levy. Paying before the 90 day mark avoids the recorded lien that can show up when a buyer's title company searches the property.

sections.h2: Buying or inheriting a Murray County house
sections.html:
A buyer should look at what the exemptions are doing for the current owner, since a homestead on the account does not move to the new owner. The buyer files a fresh application with the assessors, and the January 1 to April 1 window applies to special assessments.

The same goes for an inherited house: the heirs should ask the assessors what must be filed in their own names and ask the commissioner whether the bill has been paid. Bring proof of ownership either way.

faqs.q: When are Murray County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Normally December 1, after which interest builds at 1% a month. Manufactured homes pay by May 1.

faqs.q: Which phone line serves Murray County property tax?
faqs.a: Call (706) 517-1400. Extension 1 reaches the Tax Commissioner and extension 2 reaches the assessors.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty for paying Murray County tax late?
faqs.a: Yes. Interest of 1% accrues monthly after December 1, and 90 days later a 10% penalty arrives, except on homesteaded parcels owing under $500.

faqs.q: Can I file a Murray County homestead exemption online?
faqs.a: Yes for the regular one. Elderly exemptions need income proof, so those go in person or by mail.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff to appeal a Murray County assessment?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the notice date, by letter to the assessors. Certified mail or hand delivery is the safest route.
